name: Forehand, focused
description: A controlled swing, with elbow movement and wrist speed.
rubric: Observe a balanced base and comfortable elbow extension through preparation and follow-through. Ask for a stationary camera with the full body and right arm visible. Do not infer ball speed, racket motion, or contact from body joints.
coachPrompt: Use only actual uploaded frames and trusted measurements. State uncertainty and missing evidence. Angles are projected 2D measurements; do not diagnose injuries or claim universal ideal angles. Physical speed requires reliable height calibration. Offer one manageable drill grounded in the visible movement. Coach a right-handed squash forehand. Explain if the arm is occluded or the athlete uses the other hand.

name: Squat control
description: Look at knee and hip movement through a comfortable squat.
rubric: Use a stationary side view with the whole body visible. Observe controlled lowering and rising, foot contact, and changes in knee and hip angles. Depth and stance depend on the athlete; do not prescribe a universal angle or infer forces.
coachPrompt: Use only actual uploaded frames and trusted measurements. State uncertainty and missing evidence. Angles are projected 2D measurements; do not diagnose injuries or claim universal ideal angles. Physical speed requires reliable height calibration. Offer one manageable drill grounded in the visible movement. Coach a comfortable bodyweight squat. Only discuss the visible side and mention perspective limitations.

name: Push-up control
description: Follow elbow movement and body alignment during a push-up.
rubric: Use a stationary side view with shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips and ankles visible. Observe controlled elbow movement and shoulder–hip–ankle alignment. Encourage a comfortable range and appropriate variation, without universal depth or elbow-angle targets.
coachPrompt: Use only actual uploaded frames and trusted measurements. State uncertainty and missing evidence. Angles are projected 2D measurements; do not diagnose injuries or claim universal ideal angles. Physical speed requires reliable height calibration. Offer one manageable drill grounded in the visible movement. Coach a controlled push-up. Stop or modify movement that causes pain; avoid medical assessments.
